name: Pinnacle Financial Partners, Inc.
moat_justification: Real Southeast deposit franchise (No. 1 in Nashville, No. 4 in Atlanta) and a talent-led relationship model (Fortune Best Companies No. 12 in 2026), doubled in scale by the Synovus merger (closed Jan. 1, 2026) — capped at weak-to-moderate because banking is a commodity product with no structural pricing power and legacy returns have not cleared the cost of capital: ROE 9.31% / 7.39% / 9.11% in FY2023-25 (fundamentals.json), roic_proxy null and gross margin not presented for a bank, so no ROIC evidence supports a higher score; the combined franchise is nine months old and untested through credit stress. CAP 7.2y.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
THIN_HISTORY: only 3 fiscal years of data

DEBT_TAGS_BLANK: no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt is UNKNOWN (not zero); no leverage verdict is possible from the engine, state the balance sheet from the filing in analysis.md
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.0x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (9.5%) vs bull-case tier B (16.2%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Quality Southeast regional bank fresh off the Synovus merger, moat 4/10 — the engine's Tier S print is a merger/OCF artifact; on a TTM base ($8.69/sh, combined share count) with through-cycle growth the weighted IRR is 12.78% (IV@15% $77.47 vs $94.72), so it clears 15% only below ~$77; bank-model mismatch, confidence low.
moat_for: Deposit franchise in growth markets — No. 1 deposit share in Nashville, No. 4 in Atlanta, $129.1B combined assets across nine Southeast/mid-Atlantic states
Talent-led relationship model — No. 12 on Fortune's 100 Best Companies to Work For in 2026 (10th straight year); demonstrably hires revenue producers from larger banks
Merger scale — the Synovus combination (closed Jan. 1, 2026) roughly doubles the balance sheet and adds Georgia/Florida scale without a cash premium
Earnings momentum in the combined prints — Q2 2026 adjusted EPS $2.50 vs $2.00 a year earlier (legacy basis), NIM 3.4%
moat_against: Commodity product — deposits and loans are fungible; returns are earned through the cycle, not from structural pricing power
Returns below a moat standard — legacy ROE 7.4–9.3% over FY2023–25 (fundamentals.json) has not stayed above the cost of equity through a cycle
Credit-cycle exposure — provisions are the swing factor and OCF adds them back; a Southeast real-estate downturn hits the bear cases fast
Merger integration risk — brand transition in Florida runs through Q1 2027, merger costs cut Q1 2026 EPS to $0.89, combined franchise unproven through any credit stress
Capital-constrained growth — loan growth, dividends and buybacks compete for the same regulatory capital
